main_text.head: EXERC. XXXII.
VTRVM EPILEPSIA SIT VENTRICVLORVM cerebri obstructio?
main_text.p: AN uero morbus comitialis & fonticus sit uentriculorum cerebri obstructio, nonnulli non abs re dubitant. Si (inquiunt) obstruerentur cerebri finus, sensu & motu plane priuaret animal: quandoquidem sentiendi facultas, ac mouendi, seu spiritus animalis in singula membra haudquaquam diffunderetur, sed intus pręcluderetur. At uero singulis epilepsiæ paroxysmis epilepticorum membra uehementiori motu, quàm antea concitantur. Quod autem deprauatę moueantur, nō penuria, facultatis animalis, sed cerebri læsio in causa est. Etenim ipsum læsum omnibus membris confusę, deprauateq; imperat, necfingulis musculis quantum extendi, laxariq; debeat, præfinit. Idem sane ipsi adest, quòd & facuo, aut insano regi, qui suos subditos deprauatę regit, ac miserrimè concutit. Itaque his omnibus rite perpensis, nullam fieri finuū cerebri obstructionem in comitiali morbo, concludere rectè possumus. Adhæc in forti apoplexia, & etiam in debili omnes

page.notes: Transcription is from a faint, slightly blurred scan. The text was read with care but several words are uncertain and should be checked against the original. Note that the printed text reads "facuo" and "fingulis" and other forms as set; these are copied as the printer seems to have set them, with no emendation. The phrase "Quod" after "Quoniam" and "uentriculorum" are read as printed. The line "omnes" at the foot is a catchword-like word at the right margin and is kept in the text as the last printed word. A few words at line ends, such as "fonti-cus", "comitia-li", "deprauatę", are set with printed hyphens or broken across lines and may need confirmation of exact hyphenation. The transcription has not been checked letter by letter against a higher-resolution scan.
